items.title: Live: Trump suspends bombing for two weeks, Iran pledges safe passage through Strait of Hormuz
items.description: US President ‌Donald Trump says he ‌has agreed "to ‌suspend the bombing and attack ‌of Iran ‌for a ‌period ‌of ‌two weeks". Follow live.

items.title: Trump agrees to 'double-sided ceasefire' less than 90 minutes before deadline
items.description: Donald Trump says he has agreed to suspend US attacks on Iran for two weeks as part of a "double-sided ceasefire". Iran is claiming victory and says it will stop its attacks if the US does.

items.title: Live: ASX rallies more than 2pc as oil falls back below $US100 on Iran deal
items.description: The US president announced a two-week ceasefire, as the clock counted down to his Iran deadline. The ASX has jumped on the news, while oil futures have plunged about 15pc. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Cost of filling best-selling car up by $100 since start of Iran war
items.description: The ABC analyses how the cost of a full tank in Australia's most-purchased cars of 2025 has changed since the beginning of the Iran war.

items.title: Live: PM welcomes ceasefire but says Trump's language wasn't 'appropriate'
items.description: Anthony Albanese has described the two-week US-Iran ceasefire as positive news but says Donald Trump's rhetoric overnight wasn't appropriate. Follow live.

items.title: Ben Roberts-Smith to remain in custody on war crimes charges
items.description: War veteran Ben Roberts-Smith will remain in custody after his lawyers made no application for bail and a court adjourned his criminal case until June.

items.title: Vance calls Trump as US rallies for Viktor Orbán
items.description: US President Donald Trump has sent his vice-president to Hungary in a bid to salvage the political future of far-right leader Viktor Orbán, who is flailing in the polls days before a closely watched election.

items.title: Farmers angered by plans to turn coal mine into lake bigger than Sydney Harbour
items.description: There are plans to turn the former Hazelwood coal mine in Victoria into a lake bigger than Sydney Harbour, but farmers and environmentalists are worried about the impact on nearby waterways.

items.title: Where cattle once roamed, conservation now grows — and so do concerns
items.description: Hailed as a win for the environment, $200 million has been spent purchasing new national parks in outback NSW — but not everyone is celebrating.

items.title: Husband's dying wish for more kids an impossible choice in childcare desert
items.description: In the depths of grief, this family wants to grow. But a childcare crisis stands in its way.

items.title: Man charged over Queensland hate speech laws faces court
items.description: Liam Parry, 33, was arrested and charged last month for reciting the banned phrase "from the river to the sea."

items.title: Smallest town in Australia for sale as two residents decide to sell roadhouse
items.description: Cooladdi, nine hours west of Brisbane, dwindled in population when its railway station closed, but it continues to attract road-trippers and graziers. Its owners run local services including a shop, motel and mail service.

items.title: Body found on rural Victorian property during search for missing man
items.description: Police have discovered the body of a man on a property east of Ouyen in regional Victoria.

items.title: 'A worker is going to be stabbed': Union airs hospital safety concerns
items.description: NT Health has rejected calls for a security review at Royal Darwin Hospital's busy emergency department amid threats against staff, with staff concerned "a worker is going to be stabbed".

items.title: 'I just had to do it for me': The ambiguous loss of family estrangement
items.description: Estrangement usually begins after a significant traumatic experience with a loved one, experts say.

items.title: Quiz: Pack your suitcase, we're going on a trip
items.description: Which European microstate is smaller? And which US president isn’t on Mount Rushmore?

items.title: Team behind cult 2012 video game reunites on Grammy winner
items.description: Art director Matt Nava and composer Austin Wintory reveal how their cult 2012 video game Journey shaped their latest offering, the Grammy Award-winning Sword of the Sea.

items.title: Why this photo shoot made rugby star Mel Kawa feel like a fraud
items.description: Recently retired rugby union player Mel Kawa regularly broke down in tears, grappling with her love of the game and the $2,000 she was paid to play it.

items.title: Water storage feud heats up as frustrated farmers take on corporate giants
items.description: Central Queensland irrigators are demanding a "fair go" from two mega water users that are pumping from a ratepayer-owned storage without paying anything for its multimillion-dollar costs.

items.title: Court sets aside convictions of parents for starving daughter, grants bail
items.description: A Perth man and woman who were found guilty in 2024 of starving their daughter, who weighed about 28 kilograms when she was admitted to hospital aged nearly 17, have their convictions set aside on appeal.

items.title: Tourists urged not to cancel plans as Cyclone Maila intensifies
items.description: Severe Tropical Cyclone Maila is now a category five system and is expected to cross into Far North Queensland on Sunday.

items.title: Duke to retire from Socceroos after World Cup bid
items.description: Mitch Duke will retire from international football this year, but is still hopeful of being part of Australia's FIFA World Cup squad.

items.title: Zach was behind bars in his teens. He says jails are just 'breeding criminals'
items.description: Hundreds of legal, health and children's organisations are calling on Anthony Albanese to convene an emergency summit to address the over-incarceration of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children.

items.title: Boards make decisions affecting the nation but they don't reflect modern society
items.description: There's a push to get younger people, women and more diverse community members on the boards making the big decisions in Australian life.

items.title: Matt Canavan looks to stars for 'Australia on steroids' plan
items.description: A domestic space industry, a baby boom, new dams and more factories are on Nationals leader Matt Canavan's to-do list to deliver what he describes as an Australian economic revolution.
